requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents, once every group is decided, to commit the agreed requirements of all groups in one commit before any implementation, leaving out uncommitted edits the user said do not belong to the task.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.commit` says the `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to do three things once every group is decided. They must commit the agreed requirements of all groups in one commit. They must do it before any implementation. They must leave out uncommitted edits the user said do not belong to the task.

Every clause describes what the skill's text tells agents to do. None of them prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. I tried to build an alternative that keeps the instruction but breaks a structural clause, and no such alternative exists. The same instruction could sit in any section of `SKILL.md`, in any wording, or in an included reference file, and it would still satisfy the text. So where the instruction sits and how it is worded are discretionary.

The only supplied root is `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, the whole file. Its outline has `section[Habeas%20requirements]` with children `section[Workflow]`, `section[Writing%20chapters]`, `section[Choosing%20references]`, `section[What%20the%20review%20checks]` and `section[Gotchas]`. Whether the skill actually carries this instruction is a question of its content. That is a behavioral matter for the tests or review criterion, not a structural obligation needing an {impl} marker. No implementation reference is missing and there is nothing to acknowledge.

behavioral: The requirement obliges the `habeas-requirements` skill to direct agents on three points. They commit only once every group is decided. They commit all groups' agreed requirements in one commit before any implementation. They leave out uncommitted edits the user said do not belong to the task. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_commits_every_group_together_before_code]` is marked `{test}` for it and covers each point against the bundled skill text.

- **One commit, all groups, before code.** `step_of(SKILL, "then commit it, all groups together, before any code")` must find a workflow step containing that phrase. It panics if none does. In `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` this is step 5, "Commit", which says to commit "all groups together, before any code". Dropping or altering the wording fails the test.
- **Only once every group is decided.** `assert!(commit > step_of(SKILL, "**Gate:**"))` requires the commit step to come after the Gate step. The Gate step forbids a commit until every group is agreed, rejected or deferred. A skill that moved the commit ahead of the gate would fail.
- **Leaving out edits that do not belong.** `step(SKILL, commit).contains("leave out unrelated edits found in step 1")` requires the commit step itself to carry the exclusion. It ties the exclusion to the edits step 1 found and asked the user about. The separate test `the_requirements_skill_asks_about_foreign_edits_before_drafting` covers step 1's ask-the-user behaviour, so it need not be repeated here.

The unmarked test `the_requirements_skill_commits_agreed_requirements_before_code` also asserts the full ordering `draft < review < gate < commit < implement`. It is marked for the parent requirement, not this one, and the marked test does not depend on it. The "before any code" obligation is already checked through the commit step's required phrase. I found no obligation that lacks a test and no gap.
